metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Rules apply only to outside contributions to Ghostty; maintainers are exempt and may use AI at their discretion.

evidence.quote: All AI usage in any form must be disclosed.
The human-in-the-loop must fully understand all code.
Issues and discussions can use AI assistance but must have a full human-in-the-loop.
These rules apply only to outside contributions to Ghostty. Maintainers are exempt from these rules and may use AI tools at their discretion

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named; only obligations on the contributor
domains.reasoning: The policy names code/PR/issue/discussion contributions explicitly and states clear supervision requirements (mandatory disclosure of tool and extent, and a human-in-the-loop who must fully understand/edit the work), plus a scope limit exempting maintainers. However it never states who is accountable for the resulting output - the human-in-the-loop obligation is a duty, not an assignment of responsibility - so accountability_holder is not_specified, keeping this at 'partial' rather than 'yes'.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting recording, bots, or consent for closed/small-group discussion
domains.reasoning: The policy text contains no reference to meetings, calls, recordings, or notetaker/meeting bots of any kind.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to AI-generated media: art, images, videos, audio, etc.; text and code are the only acceptable AI-generated content.

evidence.quote: No AI-generated media is allowed (art, images, videos, audio, etc.). Text and code are the only acceptable AI-generated content, per the other rules in this policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-generated content/media decisions
domains.reasoning: The policy explicitly names design-asset-type content (art, images, video, audio) and sets a clear ban on AI generation of it, satisfying supervision level and scope, but never states who is accountable for content that is or isn't compliant, so it stays 'partial'. Documentation/blog text is not separately named beyond the general 'text' carve-out.

evidence.quote: People who produce bad contributions that are clearly AI (slop) will be added to our public denouncement list.

domains.rationale_only_mention: It is rude and disrespectful to approach this boundary with low-effort, unqualified work, since it puts the burden of validation on the maintainer.
domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on whether/how AI may be used in moderation actions themselves
domains.reasoning: The denouncement-list clause is an enforcement consequence for misusing AI in contributions, not a rule about AI's role in moderation actions, and the maintainer-burden language is offered as rationale for the contribution rules rather than a moderation rule itself. No supervision level or accountability holder is stated for AI use in moderation.

evidence.quote: Every discussion, issue, and pull request is read and reviewed by humans (and sometimes machines, too).

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for machine-assisted review
domains.reasoning: The policy names machine involvement in review explicitly ('and sometimes machines, too') but sets no rule about how AI may review, whether it must be advisory-only, or who is accountable, leaving the domain named but unspecified - 'partial'.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous or agentic AI acting on the repository
domains.reasoning: There is no mention of agents, bots, or autonomous AI systems acting on the repository without a human driving them; the whole policy is framed around a human 'driver' of AI tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on energy/water/carbon impact of AI tool use
domains.reasoning: No text in the policy references energy use, water use, carbon footprint, or hardware footprint as a concern or rule.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on server load or hardware/financing cost from AI use
domains.reasoning: The policy discusses maintainer time burden but never mentions server load, hardware costs, or financing strain, which is the infrastructure domain's defined scope.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on Ghostty's own content/data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The policy never addresses whether Ghostty's issues, discussions, code, or user data may be used to train AI models; its focus is entirely on contributors' use of AI tools, not the project's data being consumed for training.

unscoped_statements.quote: All AI usage in any form must be disclosed.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Ghostty sets specific, strict rules for code/text contributions (mandatory disclosure and a fully-understanding human-in-the-loop) and flatly bans AI-generated media, but never names an accountability holder in any domain, treats review only descriptively, and is entirely silent on notetaker bots, autonomous/agentic use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and use of the project's own data for training.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
